requirements.evidence: Migrations match the spec: slug unique 'entities_slug_unique', timestamps, softDeletes (create_entities_table.php:17-20); FKs cascadeOnDelete, role default 'employee', storedAs owner_seq, unique indexes 'entity_memberships_entity_user_unique' and 'entity_memberships_one_owner' (create_entity_memberships_table.php:16-23). Entity has getRouteKeyName()='slug', memberships(), users(), owner() as HasOne filtered by role (Entity.php:20-49). EntityMembership has the role cast, owner/admin/employee scopes, entity()/user() (EntityMembership.php:21-69). UserRole::manageable() returns [Admin, Employee] (UserRole.php:16-19). User::memberships/entities/membershipFor (User.php:35-56). Factories with owner/admin/employee states. Policies follow the rules: owner membership never deletable, self-removal allowed, otherwise owner/admin (EntityMembershipPolicy.php:30-46); manageSettings owner only (EntityPolicy.php:38-41). docs/database-schema.md updated to drop owner_membership_id. Backtick-quoted `role` in the generated expression works on both MariaDB and SQLite.

conventions.evidence: The conventions say 'No production code without a test; everything implemented ships with a test', and the diff adds no test files. Things done right: migrations have reversible down() and timestamped generator-style names, $fillable is set deliberately (Entity.php:20, EntityMembership.php:16), authorization lives in app/Policies, and CHANGELOG plus docs/database-schema.md were updated.

security.evidence: Policies deny non-members by default (membershipFor null -> false at EntityPolicy.php:26-28 and EntityMembershipPolicy.php:21-23, 40-42). The owner membership can never be deleted, which is checked before the self-removal branch (EntityMembershipPolicy.php:30-36). The database enforces a single owner per entity. Mass assignment is limited by $fillable. Nothing here takes user input.

tests.evidence: change.diff has no tests/ files. Nothing covers the migrations (unique slug, the one-owner constraint, multiple non-owners), the models and factories, or the policy matrix, including the non-member and owner-deletion denial paths.

simplicity.evidence: Lean, direct models and policies, and EntityPolicy::delete reuses update() (EntityPolicy.php:33-36). Small redundancies: the private roleOf() helper does tryFrom handling that the enum cast already makes unnecessary (EntityMembershipPolicy.php:47-56), and the owner/admin in_array check is repeated three times.

readability.evidence: Clear names, PHPDoc generics on relations and scopes, consistent factory style. The roleOf() helper is used inconsistently: delete() uses it while other methods read ->role directly. Some generics omit $this (HasMany<EntityMembership> at Entity.php:27 vs BelongsTo<Entity, $this> at EntityMembership.php:53).

scope.evidence: Only the migrations, models, enum, factories, policies, CHANGELOG and docs/database-schema.md are touched. No routes, middleware, session or UI. Removing locale_default from the ER diagram (database-schema.md:504) is a small doc edit that goes slightly past what the task asked.

issues.explanation: The change ships no Pest/PHPUnit tests for the migrations, the single-owner DB constraint, the factories, the relations or either policy, which breaks the project's mandatory TDD rule.
The roleOf() helper re-parses a role that is already cast to UserRole, and only delete() uses it, so role handling is inconsistent across the policy.
The owner-or-admin check `in_array($role, [UserRole::Owner, UserRole::Admin], true)` is repeated in three places; a small helper (e.g. on the enum) would remove the duplication.
The proposed `locale_default` column was removed from the ER diagram even though the task only asked to replace `owner_membership_id`.
The relation generics leave out the `$this` parameter, unlike the BelongsTo annotations in EntityMembership.php.

review.summary: The change implements the entities/entity_memberships schema with the DB-enforced single-owner index, the Entity/EntityMembership models, the UserRole enum, factories and both policies, all correctly and matching the contract, and keeps CHANGELOG and the schema doc in sync. However, it ships no tests at all, which violates the project's mandatory test-first rule, so it needs changes before merging.
